description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates how the absolute mean (“Abs Mean”) of hidden states varies across model layers for three conditions: before a gate, after a gate, and a baseline. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer layers from 0 to 23 with tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to a little above 4 (with labeled ticks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4). The blue dashed line (no markers) for “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71” starts near 0.05 at layer 0, rises to around 0.25 by about layer 2, stays roughly in the 0.2–0.5 range through the mid layers (e.g., around 0.3–0.45 between roughly layers 8–17), then increases more sharply after about layer 18, reaching about 0.9 around layer 19–20, jumping to roughly 2.6 around layer 21–22, and ending near 4.4 at layer 23. The orange dotted line (no markers) for “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05” stays close to 0 in early layers, gradually increases through later layers to around 0.1 by the final layers, and shows a small dip around layer 22 before returning near ~0.1 at layer 23. The green solid line (no markers) for “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04” similarly remains near 0 in early layers and gradually rises across layers, reaching roughly ~0.1 by layer 23, with a smooth, low-amplitude upward trend throughout.
